strings.name: Andrés Iniesta
strings.summary: Andrés Iniesta was a key midfielder in Barcelona’s and Spain’s passing systems, known for control, spatial judgment and major-match performances. He scored the winner in the 2010 World Cup final, won two Euros with Spain and four Champions Leagues with Barça. After playing in Japan and the UAE, he retired in 2024 and began coaching Gulf United in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: The World Cup final’s winning scorer and a central figure in Barcelona’s possession football.

strings.highlights.h1.title: World Cup final winner
strings.highlights.h1.text: His extra-time goal delivered Spain’s first World Cup in 2010.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Passing system and titles
strings.highlights.h2.text: A Barça midfield cornerstone with four Champions Leagues; Euro 2012 player of the tournament.
strings.timeline.t1.title: First head-coaching role
strings.timeline.t1.text: Became Gulf United head coach in Dubai while continuing professional coaching training.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Playing retirement
strings.timeline.t2.text: Ended his professional playing career after a final spell at Emirates Club.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Move to Kobe
strings.timeline.t3.text: Left Barça for Vissel Kobe and ended his Spain career that year.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Euro player of the tournament
strings.timeline.t4.text: Helped Spain retain the European title and received the tournament’s top player award.
strings.timeline.t5.title: World Cup champion
strings.timeline.t5.text: Scored the only goal in extra time against the Netherlands in the final.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Barça treble
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won La Liga, Copa del Rey and Champions League with the team.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Barça first-team debut
strings.timeline.t7.text: Made his debut against Club Brugge in the Champions League.
strings.timeline.t8.title: La Masia arrival
strings.timeline.t8.text: Left his home youth system for Barça at twelve.
